stem: A friend asks a security professional to "just take a quick look" for weaknesses in the website of the company where the friend works. The friend has no authority over the site. What should the professional do?

options.A: Run a light, non-intrusive scan, since the friend works at the company and is trying to help
options.B: Test the site only outside business hours so that no customers are affected by any scanning
options.C: Decline unless the site owner gives written authorization
options.D: Test the site, but share the results only with the friend and not with the company itself

explanation: Testing a system without the owner's permission can be illegal and breaks professional ethics, however good the intent. Only someone with authority over the system can authorize testing.

distractor_rationales.A: Good intentions and employment do not give the friend authority to approve testing.
distractor_rationales.B: Timing does not make unauthorized testing acceptable.
distractor_rationales.D: Keeping results private does not fix the lack of authorization and could harm the owner.

stem: A colleague preparing for a security certification asks you to share the actual questions you remember from your exam. What is the appropriate response?

options.A: Share the questions, since helping others advance in the profession is encouraged
options.B: Share only the questions that you answered incorrectly on the exam
options.C: Share the questions verbally but not in writing, to avoid leaving a record
options.D: Decline, and point the colleague to the official study materials instead

explanation: Certification candidates agree not to disclose exam content. Sharing questions breaches that agreement and the code of ethics, and undermines the credential's value.

distractor_rationales.A: Helping peers is encouraged, but not by breaking an exam nondisclosure agreement.
distractor_rationales.B: Disclosing any exam content breaches the agreement.
distractor_rationales.C: The medium does not matter; disclosure is still a breach.

stem: Ransomware encrypts a clinic's scheduling database. Investigators confirm that no data left the network. Which security property was MOST directly affected?

options.A: Availability
options.B: Confidentiality of the patient appointment records stored in the database
options.C: Nonrepudiation of the staff members who booked the appointments
options.D: Authenticity of the software that runs the clinic's scheduling system

explanation: The data was not disclosed, but staff can no longer use it. Loss of access to systems and data is an availability impact.

distractor_rationales.B: With no data taken, confidentiality was not the main impact.
distractor_rationales.C: Nonrepudiation concerns proof of who performed an action.
distractor_rationales.D: Nothing indicates the software itself was not genuine.

stem: What is the main purpose of an information security steering committee?

options.A: To perform the daily monitoring of security alerts from across the enterprise
options.B: To align security priorities with business strategy across departments
options.C: To write and maintain the configuration standards for all network devices
options.D: To conduct penetration tests of new applications before they go live

explanation: A steering committee brings together leaders from across the business to set security direction, approve priorities, and resolve conflicts so security supports business goals.

distractor_rationales.A: Alert monitoring is a security operations function.
distractor_rationales.C: Configuration standards are written by technical teams.
distractor_rationales.D: Penetration testing is performed by testers, not a governance committee.

stem: A merchant must comply with the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS). What type of obligation is this for the merchant?

options.A: A criminal statute passed by a national legislature
options.B: A regulation issued by a government agency
options.C: A contractual obligation enforced through card brand agreements
options.D: A voluntary guideline with no consequences for noncompliance

explanation: PCI DSS is an industry standard. Merchants are bound to it by their agreements with acquiring banks and card brands, which can impose fines or end card acceptance.

distractor_rationales.A: PCI DSS is not a law passed by a legislature.
distractor_rationales.B: It is not issued by a government regulator, although some laws reference it.
distractor_rationales.D: Noncompliance carries real contractual consequences.

references_topic: PCI DSS as a contractual obligation

stem: A newsletter signup form asks for name, email, birth date, gender, and household income, although only the email is needed to send the newsletter. Which privacy principle does this form violate?

options.A: Accuracy of personal data
options.B: Storage limitation
options.C: Transparency to data subjects
options.D: Data minimization

explanation: Data minimization means collecting only the personal data needed for the stated purpose. The extra fields are unnecessary for sending a newsletter.

distractor_rationales.A: Accuracy concerns keeping data correct, not how much is collected.
distractor_rationales.B: Storage limitation concerns how long data is kept.
distractor_rationales.C: Transparency concerns telling people how their data is used.

stem: Which form of intellectual property protection applies to a company's brand name and logo?

options.A: Trademark
options.B: Patent covering the company's novel inventions and manufacturing processes
options.C: Trade secret covering confidential formulas known only to employees
options.D: Copyright covering the company's written documentation and source code

explanation: Trademarks protect names, logos, and other marks that identify the source of goods or services.

distractor_rationales.B: Patents protect inventions, not brand names.
distractor_rationales.C: Trade secrets protect confidential business information.
distractor_rationales.D: Copyright protects original works of authorship, not brand identifiers.

stem: Two companies disagree over whether one breached a contract to deliver secure software. Which type of investigation supports this dispute?

options.A: Criminal investigation
options.B: Civil investigation
options.C: Administrative investigation
options.D: Regulatory investigation

explanation: Disputes between private parties, such as breach of contract claims, are civil matters and are decided on the preponderance of the evidence.

distractor_rationales.A: Criminal investigations concern violations of criminal law prosecuted by the state.
distractor_rationales.C: Administrative investigations are internal, such as employee policy violations.
distractor_rationales.D: Regulatory investigations are driven by a government agency's authority.

stem: What is the term for the minimum security configuration that every system of a given type must meet, such as all Windows servers?

options.A: Guideline
options.B: Policy
options.C: Baseline
options.D: Procedure

explanation: A baseline defines the minimum security settings required for a category of systems. Systems may exceed it but must not fall below it.

distractor_rationales.A: Guidelines are recommendations, not mandatory minimums.
distractor_rationales.B: Policies are high-level statements of intent.
distractor_rationales.D: Procedures are step-by-step instructions for performing tasks.

stem: A business can tolerate losing no more than four hours of transaction data. Which approach meets this recovery point objective?

options.A: Nightly backups at midnight retained for thirty days
options.B: Weekly full backups with daily differential backups in between
options.C: A recovery site that can be running within four hours of a disaster
options.D: Backups or replication at least every four hours

explanation: The RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time, so data must be captured at least every four hours.

distractor_rationales.A: Nightly backups could lose up to 24 hours of data.
distractor_rationales.B: Daily differentials could still lose a full day of data.
distractor_rationales.C: Being running within four hours describes the recovery time objective, not the RPO.

stem: Which document do new employees typically sign at onboarding to confirm they understand how they may and may not use company systems?

options.A: Acceptable use policy
options.B: Business impact analysis
options.C: Service level agreement with the organization's main vendors
options.D: Disaster recovery plan for the primary data center

explanation: An acceptable use policy defines permitted and prohibited use of company systems, and signing it records the employee's acknowledgment.

distractor_rationales.B: A business impact analysis assesses the effect of disruptions.
distractor_rationales.C: SLAs define service commitments between organizations.
distractor_rationales.D: A disaster recovery plan covers restoring systems after a disaster.

stem: A server farm is valued at $500,000. A fire would destroy 30% of its value. What is the single loss expectancy (SLE)?
explanation: SLE = asset value × exposure factor = $500,000 × 0.30 = $150,000.

distractor_rationales.A: $350,000 is the value that would remain, not the loss.
distractor_rationales.C: $15,000 misplaces the decimal point.
distractor_rationales.D: $1,666,667 divides by the exposure factor instead of multiplying.

stem: Which control PRIMARILY supports integrity rather than confidentiality?

options.A: Encrypting laptops so that data on lost devices cannot be read
options.B: Classifying documents so that staff know who may view them
options.C: File integrity monitoring that alerts on unauthorized changes
options.D: Privacy screens that stop onlookers from reading a display

explanation: File integrity monitoring detects unauthorized modification of files, which is an integrity concern.

distractor_rationales.A: Disk encryption protects confidentiality.
distractor_rationales.B: Classification guides who may see data, supporting confidentiality.
distractor_rationales.D: Privacy screens prevent disclosure, supporting confidentiality.

stem: Payment data is encrypted and access is restricted, yet an authorized clerk changed vendor bank details and diverted a payment. Which control would MOST directly have prevented this?

options.A: Stronger encryption of the payment database using longer key lengths
options.B: Moving the payment system to a separate network segment behind a firewall
options.C: Sending the clerk to additional security awareness training on phishing
options.D: Requiring a second person to approve changes to vendor bank details

explanation: The failure was an integrity problem caused by an authorized insider. Dual control on sensitive changes means one person cannot alter payment details alone.

distractor_rationales.A: Encryption protects confidentiality, and the clerk was already authorized.
distractor_rationales.B: Segmentation does not stop an authorized user.
distractor_rationales.C: Phishing training does not address insider changes.

stem: A CISO is asked to brief the board on security. What should the briefing focus on?

options.A: Key risks in business terms, compared with the board's risk appetite
options.B: The number of firewall rules changed and patches applied last quarter
options.C: A detailed walk-through of the latest malware reverse-engineering results
options.D: The technical specifications of the tools the security team plans to buy

explanation: Boards govern risk. They need to understand the most important risks, their business impact, and whether the organization is within its appetite, so they can make decisions.

distractor_rationales.B: Activity counts do not tell the board whether risk is acceptable.
distractor_rationales.C: Malware analysis detail is too technical for board decisions.
distractor_rationales.D: Tool specifications are management detail, not board-level information.

stem: Before acquiring a smaller company, the buyer's security team reviews the target's breach history, security controls, and open audit findings. Which concept does this review demonstrate?

options.A: Due care, because the buyer is fixing the target's weaknesses before the deal closes
options.B: Due diligence
options.C: Risk transfer, because the target's risks move to the seller's insurer
options.D: Separation of duties between the two companies' security teams

explanation: Due diligence is investigating and understanding risk before acting. Assessing the target before the deal is exactly that.

distractor_rationales.A: Due care is acting on known risks; this review gathers information before any action.
distractor_rationales.C: Nothing here transfers risk to an insurer.
distractor_rationales.D: Separation of duties splits tasks among people to prevent fraud.

stem: A company must comply with several overlapping security regulations and customer contracts, and each audit team tests the same controls separately. What is the BEST way to reduce this duplication?

options.A: Choose the single regulation with the largest fines and comply only with that one
options.B: Assign a separate compliance team for each regulation so each can work independently
options.C: Map all requirements to one set of controls and test each control once
options.D: Ask the regulators to accept the company's own summary instead of an audit

explanation: A common control framework maps many requirements to a single control set, so each control is implemented and evidenced once and reused across audits.

distractor_rationales.A: Ignoring other obligations creates noncompliance.
distractor_rationales.B: Separate teams increase duplication.
distractor_rationales.D: Regulators decide how they assess compliance.

stem: An auditor asks for proof that quarterly access reviews were performed last year. Which evidence is BEST?

options.A: A statement from the IT manager confirming that the reviews took place as planned
options.B: The access review policy document describing how often reviews should be done
options.C: A screenshot of the review tool's home page taken on the day of the audit
options.D: Dated review records showing reviewers' decisions and resulting removals

explanation: Dated records with reviewer decisions and follow-up actions show that each review actually happened and was acted on.

distractor_rationales.A: A verbal or written assurance is weak evidence.
distractor_rationales.B: A policy shows intent, not performance.
distractor_rationales.C: A current screenshot says nothing about last year's reviews.

stem: Analysts replace customer names with random tokens, while a separate team keeps the table that maps tokens back to names. How should this data set be treated?

options.A: As pseudonymized personal data that still needs protection
options.B: As anonymous data that is no longer subject to privacy law
options.C: As public data that can be published without restriction
options.D: As encrypted data that can be shared freely with any vendor

explanation: Because the mapping table exists, the data can be re-identified. Pseudonymization reduces risk, but the data is still personal data.

distractor_rationales.B: True anonymization is irreversible, which is not the case here.
distractor_rationales.C: Pseudonymized data is not public.
distractor_rationales.D: Tokenization is not encryption, and the data still needs controlled sharing.

stem: Which statement about patents is TRUE?

options.A: They protect an invention indefinitely as long as it is kept confidential by the owner
options.B: They grant exclusive rights for a limited term in exchange for public disclosure
options.C: They protect the expression of an idea, such as source code, from being copied
options.D: They protect a company's logo and product names used in the marketplace

explanation: A patent gives its owner exclusive rights to an invention for a limited period, typically about 20 years, in exchange for publicly disclosing how it works.

distractor_rationales.A: Indefinite protection through secrecy describes a trade secret.
distractor_rationales.C: Protecting the expression of an idea describes copyright.
distractor_rationales.D: Logos and names are protected by trademarks.

stem: After customer data is stolen, the company receives an extortion demand threatening to publish the data. What should the security team do?

options.A: Pay quickly and quietly, since involving outsiders will only increase the damage
options.B: Contact the attackers directly to negotiate a lower price before telling anyone
options.C: Escalate to legal counsel and senior management to decide on involving law enforcement
options.D: Ignore the demand, since responding in any way encourages further extortion

explanation: Extortion is a crime, and the decision to involve law enforcement has legal and business consequences. Counsel and senior management should make it with the facts in hand.

distractor_rationales.A: Paying without legal input may break laws and does not guarantee deletion.
distractor_rationales.B: Unilateral negotiation bypasses leadership and legal advice.
distractor_rationales.D: Ignoring the demand skips required legal and notification decisions.

stem: The security policy was last updated six years ago and refers to technologies the company no longer uses. What is the BEST long-term fix?

options.A: Rewrite the policy now and then leave it unchanged until the next audit finding
options.B: Delete the policy, since the technical standards already cover the same material
options.C: Ask each department to write its own policy that matches its current technology
options.D: Review the policy on a set schedule and after major changes, keeping it technology-neutral

explanation: Policies should be reviewed regularly and when the business changes. Keeping them free of specific technologies means they stay valid while standards change underneath.

distractor_rationales.A: A one-time rewrite repeats the problem.
distractor_rationales.B: Standards depend on policy for authority and direction.
distractor_rationales.C: Separate departmental policies create inconsistency.

stem: Which type of document is high-level, technology-neutral, and approved by senior management?

options.A: Policy
options.B: Standard specifying approved encryption algorithms
options.C: Procedure describing how to reset a user's password
options.D: Guideline recommending good practices for home Wi-Fi

explanation: Policies state management's intent and direction at a high level. Standards, procedures, and guidelines add the specific detail beneath them.

distractor_rationales.B: Standards are specific and often name technologies.
distractor_rationales.C: Procedures are detailed step-by-step instructions.
distractor_rationales.D: Guidelines are optional recommendations.

stem: A senior network administrator resigns with two weeks' notice to join a competitor. What is the BEST approach during the notice period?

options.A: Leave all access in place so the administrator can finish every open project
options.B: Reduce privileged access to what handover needs and increase monitoring
options.C: Escort the administrator out immediately and cancel the notice period
options.D: Ask the administrator to promise not to take any company data

explanation: A departing privileged user is a higher risk. Limiting access to what is needed for handover, with closer monitoring, balances continuity with protection.

distractor_rationales.A: Full access leaves unnecessary exposure during a risky period.
distractor_rationales.C: Immediate removal may be justified in some cases but is not the default for a voluntary resignation.
distractor_rationales.D: A promise is not a control.

stem: What is a common weakness of purely quantitative risk analysis?

options.A: It cannot express risk in monetary terms that executives understand
options.B: It ignores the value of assets when estimating the size of losses
options.C: It relies on accurate probability and loss data that is often unavailable
options.D: It can only be performed by external auditors under professional standards

explanation: Quantitative analysis needs reliable numbers for asset values, exposure, and frequency. When data is sparse, the precise-looking results can be misleading.

distractor_rationales.A: Monetary results are a strength of quantitative analysis.
distractor_rationales.B: Asset value is central to quantitative analysis.
distractor_rationales.D: Internal teams can perform quantitative analysis.

stem: A company buys a cyber insurance policy that covers the costs of breach response and notification. Which risk response is this?

options.A: Risk avoidance
options.B: Risk acceptance
options.C: Risk mitigation
options.D: Risk transfer

explanation: Insurance shifts the financial impact of a loss to a third party, which is risk transfer. The company still owns the risk and its reputational effects.

distractor_rationales.A: Avoidance stops the activity that creates the risk.
distractor_rationales.B: Acceptance keeps the risk without further action.
distractor_rationales.C: Mitigation reduces likelihood or impact with controls.

stem: The board has set a low appetite for regulatory risk. A project team proposes accepting a high compliance risk to meet a launch date. What should the security manager do?

options.A: Escalate the decision, since it exceeds the board's stated appetite
options.B: Accept the risk on the team's behalf so the launch date can be met
options.C: Approve the launch and schedule a compliance review for next year
options.D: Ask the team to downgrade the risk rating so it fits the appetite

explanation: A risk above the organization's appetite cannot be accepted at project level. It must go to leadership with authority to accept it or require treatment.

distractor_rationales.B: The security manager does not have authority to accept risk beyond appetite.
distractor_rationales.C: Deferring review leaves a known high risk in place.
distractor_rationales.D: Changing the rating to fit hides the risk.

stem: Customers of an online store can place orders, but the system keeps no reliable record of who placed each one. A customer denies placing an order, and the store cannot prove otherwise. Which STRIDE category describes this threat?

options.A: Tampering
options.B: Repudiation
options.C: Information disclosure
options.D: Denial of service

explanation: Repudiation is the ability to deny having performed an action because there is no trustworthy evidence. Secure logging and signatures address it.

distractor_rationales.A: Tampering is unauthorized modification of data.
distractor_rationales.C: Information disclosure is exposure of data to unauthorized parties.
distractor_rationales.D: Denial of service makes a system unavailable.

stem: When threat modeling from a data flow diagram, where should the team look MOST closely for threats?

options.A: Inside a single process where no data enters or leaves at any time
options.B: At the icons used to represent external users in the diagram legend
options.C: Where data crosses trust boundaries between components
options.D: At the storage devices that are fully encrypted at rest

explanation: Trust boundaries are where data moves between zones of different privilege, such as from the internet to an application. Most attacks target these crossings.

distractor_rationales.A: A process with no inputs or outputs presents little attack surface.
distractor_rationales.B: Diagram notation is not a source of threats.
distractor_rationales.D: Encrypted storage still matters, but boundary crossings are where threats concentrate.

references_topic: Trust boundaries in data flow diagrams

stem: Attackers are sending convincing fake invoices and CEO payment requests to the finance team. General annual awareness training has not stopped the losses. What is the BEST next step?

options.A: Repeat the same general awareness training every month for all employees
options.B: Block all email from outside the organization to the finance team
options.C: Publicly name employees who pay fraudulent invoices as a deterrent
options.D: Give finance staff targeted training plus a required call-back to verify payment changes

explanation: Role-specific training for the people targeted, backed by a verification procedure, addresses business email compromise directly.

distractor_rationales.A: More generic training does not address the specific attack.
distractor_rationales.B: Blocking all external email would stop legitimate business.
distractor_rationales.C: Shaming discourages reporting and undermines a just culture.

references_topic: Targeted training for business email compromise

stem: Management asks the security team to track employees' phone locations around the clock, including off duty. Local law allows it. What should the security professional do?

options.A: Advise limiting tracking to work needs, since legal is not the same as ethical
options.B: Implement it as requested, since the law allows it and management has decided
options.C: Refuse and report management to the regulator, since tracking is illegal
options.D: Implement it quietly without telling employees to avoid complaints

explanation: Ethics can require more than the law. The professional should advise limiting collection to legitimate business needs and being transparent, while respecting management's final authority.

distractor_rationales.B: Legality alone does not make excessive monitoring appropriate.
distractor_rationales.C: The scenario states it is legal, so a regulator report is unfounded.
distractor_rationales.D: Secret monitoring deepens the ethical problem.

stem: After a cloud storage bucket was left public, the infrastructure team and the application team each said the other was responsible for its configuration. What should happen FIRST?

options.A: Discipline both team leads so that each team takes the issue seriously
options.B: Have management define and document ownership, for example in a RACI chart
options.C: Move all cloud resources to on-premises servers where ownership is clearer
options.D: Ask the security team to take over configuration of every cloud resource

explanation: The root cause is unclear accountability. Management should assign ownership explicitly so every resource has a responsible and accountable party.

distractor_rationales.A: Discipline does not fix the gap in ownership.
distractor_rationales.C: Moving off the cloud is disproportionate and does not assign ownership.
distractor_rationales.D: Centralizing all configuration in security creates a bottleneck and blurs accountability.

stem: A vendor advisory warned of a critical flaw in a company's VPN appliance. The company logged the advisory but did not patch or mitigate for nine months, and attackers then used the flaw to steal customer data. What is the company's MAIN legal exposure?

options.A: None, since the company performed due diligence by logging the advisory
options.B: Only the vendor is liable, because the flaw was in the vendor's product
options.C: Negligence, because it knew the risk and failed to exercise due care
options.D: Criminal liability for the attackers' actions carried out using the VPN

explanation: Knowing about a risk and failing to act reasonably on it is a failure of due care, which supports a negligence claim.

distractor_rationales.A: Logging the advisory is awareness; failing to act on it is the problem.
distractor_rationales.B: The vendor's flaw does not excuse the company's failure to act on a known fix.
distractor_rationales.D: The company is not criminally liable for the attackers' crimes.

stem: A customer submits a request to see all personal data the company holds about them. The data is spread across twelve systems. What should the privacy team do FIRST?

options.A: Export every table from all twelve systems and send them to the customer
options.B: Reply that the data is too spread out to collect in a reasonable time
options.C: Send only the data from the main customer database and close the request
options.D: Verify the requester's identity, then use the data inventory to locate the data

explanation: Verifying identity prevents disclosing data to an impostor. A data inventory then shows where the person's data lives, so the response is complete and limited to that person.

distractor_rationales.A: Exporting whole tables would disclose other people's data.
distractor_rationales.B: Difficulty does not remove the obligation to respond.
distractor_rationales.C: A partial response fails the request.

stem: Business units rate risks with different scales and definitions, so leadership cannot compare them in the enterprise risk register. What is the BEST fix?

options.A: Adopt one rating method with defined likelihood and impact criteria for everyone
options.B: Let each unit keep its scale, but convert every rating to "medium" for reporting
options.C: Remove the likelihood rating from the register and track only the impact rating
options.D: Ask the external auditors to re-rate all of the risks once each year

explanation: A common methodology with defined criteria makes ratings comparable, so leadership can prioritize across the whole organization.

distractor_rationales.B: Flattening ratings hides real differences.
distractor_rationales.C: Dropping likelihood loses half of the risk picture.
distractor_rationales.D: Annual external re-rating does not fix day-to-day consistency and removes ownership.

stem: Two years ago, leadership formally accepted the risk of an unpatched internal legacy server. The server has since been exposed to the internet for a new partner service. What should happen?

options.A: Nothing, since the risk was formally accepted and signed off by leadership
options.B: Reassess the risk, since the original acceptance no longer reflects the exposure
options.C: Patch the server immediately without informing the partner or leadership
options.D: Move the acceptance paperwork into the new project's documentation folder

explanation: Risk acceptance is based on conditions at the time. When exposure changes significantly, the risk must be reassessed and a new decision made.

distractor_rationales.A: The acceptance assumed internal-only exposure, which is no longer true.
distractor_rationales.C: Remediation may be right, but the decision needs reassessment and communication.
distractor_rationales.D: Moving paperwork does not address the changed risk.

stem: A company's order process depends on a third-party payment gateway, but the business impact analysis lists only internal systems. What is the BEST correction?

options.A: Remove the order process from the BIA, since part of it is outside the company's control
options.B: Assume the payment gateway provider will handle any outage without the company's help
options.C: Add upstream dependencies, including vendors, to the BIA and continuity plans
options.D: Build an in-house payment gateway to replace the provider within one year

explanation: A BIA must capture every dependency a critical process needs, including external providers, so continuity plans cover their failure.

distractor_rationales.A: Dropping a critical process from the BIA leaves it unplanned.
distractor_rationales.B: Assuming the provider will cope ignores the company's own continuity needs.
distractor_rationales.D: Rebuilding the service is disproportionate and does not fix the analysis gap.

stem: A cloud vendor that processes the company's customer data uses several subcontractors, which the company learned about only by accident. What contract provision BEST addresses this?

options.A: A clause requiring the vendor to send an annual thank-you letter to the company
options.B: A lower monthly fee in exchange for the vendor's freedom to choose subcontractors
options.C: A requirement that the company audit each subcontractor directly every month
options.D: Disclosure and approval of subprocessors, with security terms flowed down

explanation: The company must know who handles its data and ensure the same protections apply. Disclosure, approval rights, and flow-down clauses extend oversight to fourth parties.

distractor_rationales.A: A thank-you letter provides no oversight.
distractor_rationales.B: Trading oversight for a discount increases risk.
distractor_rationales.C: Monthly direct audits of every subcontractor are impractical.

stem: A small third-party risk team must oversee 500 vendors. What is the BEST approach?

options.A: Tier vendors by data access and criticality, and assess the highest tiers most deeply
options.B: Send the same long questionnaire to all 500 vendors every year and review each one
options.C: Review vendors in alphabetical order until the team runs out of time each year
options.D: Assess only the vendors that have reported a security breach in the past

explanation: Risk-based tiering puts limited effort where the exposure is greatest, with lighter review for low-risk vendors.

distractor_rationales.B: Treating every vendor the same wastes effort and overwhelms the team.
distractor_rationales.C: Alphabetical order ignores risk.
distractor_rationales.D: Past breaches are only one signal; high-risk vendors without breaches would be missed.

stem: Development teams ignore generic security training, and security reviews keep finding the same flaws. What is the BEST way to improve secure development behavior?

options.A: Require each developer to repeat the same generic training module every month
options.B: Build a security champions program with role-based training for developers
options.C: Withhold bonuses from teams whose code has any security findings at all
options.D: Have the security team rewrite all code before release to fix the flaws

explanation: Champions embedded in each team, supported by role-specific training, bring security knowledge into daily work and scale the security team's reach.

distractor_rationales.A: Repeating generic training that already failed will not change behavior.
distractor_rationales.C: Harsh penalties discourage reporting and collaboration.
distractor_rationales.D: Central rewriting does not scale and does not build developer skill.
